A1.justification: Both PDFs clearly describe Coarse Correspondences, and their main text, equations, tables and figures support comparison. V1 includes Appendices A–D. V2 ends with references and mentions supplementary EgoSchema analyses and diagnostic-data curation details that are not included, limiting comparison of that material.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark experiments, SOT diagnostic results, prompting ablations and qualitative case studies, including appendix examples.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark experiments and reports additional navigation, fine-tuned LLaVA and SQA3D transfer results.

M1.justification: The four-step correspondence-prompting algorithm remains unchanged. V2 adds substantial adaptations: an online navigation procedure using SAMv2, episodic history and action outputs, and LLaVA fine-tuning with correspondence-marked ScanQA inputs before inference. These extend the procedure beyond v1's training-free question-answering framework.

E1.justification: V2 adds R2R navigation in VLN-CE and out-of-domain SQA3D evaluation. ScanQA, OpenEQA and EgoSchema remain. V1's ten-scene, fifty-question SOT diagnostic is substantially matched by v2's camera-motion analysis; its reframing does not establish a wholly new dataset.

E2.justification: The ScanQA comparison changes substantially: v2 Table 1 adds ScanQA and ScanRefer+MCAN, replaces the original LLaVA baseline with a fine-tuned LLaVA comparison, and omits Flamingo, BLIP2 and the Gemini/Claude comparisons with and without CC. OpenEQA and EgoSchema retain their comparator sets. NavGPT supplies navigation prompts but is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: New protocols include 100 R2R val-unseen episodes, sequential action selection, five navigation metrics and a three-meter stopping criterion. V2 also introduces 64-frame fine-tuned LLaVA evaluation and SQA3D training-only versus training-and-inference controls. OpenEQA's metric description changes from accuracy to mean GPT-4 grading, although its table values remain unchanged and no rerun is established.

E4.justification: V2 adds controlled analysis of CC during training alone versus training and inference, together with transfer to unseen SQA3D. The camera-motion test and mark-design ablations are retained. V1's separate perspective-taking breakdown, two-frame diagnostic comparison, and appendix counting, relative-location and hand-drawn-mark case studies are absent from the supplied v2. The qualitative comparison against other prompting methods is reused.

E5.justification: V2 Section 5 newly states that each diagnostic question was tested 20 times, producing 1,000 trials for each sequence direction, with average accuracies reported. V1 does not disclose these repetition counts. The unchanged retained scores do not establish that additional runs occurred; neither version reports confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: New within-v2 comparisons include R2R success rates of 12.00 versus 23.00, fine-tuned LLaVA ScanQA CIDEr scores of 67.3 versus 74.2, and SQA3D accuracies of 36.0, 37.17 and 39.13. Retained GPT benchmark rows and four-frame camera-motion values are unchanged. Several diagnostic and ablation result entries are omitted; the eight-mark ROUGE-L result changes from 37.8 in v1 Table 5 to approximately 37.6 in v2 Figure 3.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, instance-frequency and area equations, ranking rule and marker-centroid equation are unchanged. Neither version develops formal theorems or proofs. V1's appendix discussions of SlowFast and Eulerian/Lagrangian viewpoints are conceptual explanations.

C1.justification: V2 expands the main contributions to navigation, training-assisted open-model applicability and cross-dataset transfer. V1 emphasizes its new spatial-orientation diagnostic and persistent perspective-taking failures; those are no longer central claims. The contribution therefore broadens beyond training-free prompting while reducing emphasis on the diagnostic limitations.

C2.justification: V2 presents fine-tuning as a remedy for open models' mark-reading and multi-image shortcomings, interprets training-only gains as evidence for data augmentation, and discusses missing action training as a navigation limitation. The supplied v2 omits v1's explicit long-video tracking failures, below-chance perspective-taking discussion, and appendix mechanism and broader-impact discussions.

D1.justification: V2 adds limited implementation disclosures: approximately 1.2 million fine-tuning examples, marking only the ScanQA portion, SAMv2 tracking and NavGPT-derived navigation prompts. It also clarifies that the reused qualitative comparison uses a manually written question. Hardware and the project link remain unchanged. Detailed diagnostic-data curation is deferred to supplementary material absent from the supplied PDF.

R1.justification: V2 expands positioning against point-cloud inputs, specialized 3D fine-tuning, Socratic video approaches and navigation work, adding references such as PointLLM, SpatialVLM, SAM 2 and NavGPT. The supplied document drops v1's cognitive-science framing and dedicated classical/diffusion correspondence and SlowFast/Lagrangian discussions. These changes substantially revise the surrounding research context.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten. Experiments are reorganized into proprietary-model and open-model sections, ScanQA and OpenEQA discussions are combined, SOT becomes a camera-motion analysis, and related work moves near the end. V1's separate discussion and appendix structure are not retained in the supplied v2.

P2.justification: V2 switches to a two-column layout, reorganizes ScanQA Table 1 by model family, adds navigation and SQA3D tables, and converts the five-metric ablation table into three ROUGE-L bar charts. The SOT displays are reduced. The overview and qualitative prompting figures are largely reused, while v1's appendix figures are absent.

improvement.justification: The trained LLaVA extension, same-data controls and SQA3D transfer test address v1's open-model applicability gap, while navigation experiments add evidence beyond question answering. These strengthen validation beyond the unchanged GPT benchmark scores. The net gain is limited by omission of the below-chance perspective-taking analysis and explicit tracking limitation, reduced ablation reporting, and supplementary details unavailable in the supplied v2.
